width.source: Raspberry Pi RP-008146-DS-1, standard-standard 200 mm camera cable: width 16.000 +-0.10

header_thickness.source: Raspberry Pi RP-008146-DS-1, standard-standard 200 mm camera cable: contact header thickness 0.309 +-0.05

body_thickness.source: Raspberry Pi RP-008146-DS-1, standard-standard 200 mm camera cable: conductor 0.027 + two insulation layers 0.055 (derived)

exposed_contact_length.source: Raspberry Pi RP-008146-DS-1, standard-standard 200 mm camera cable: strip length 5.000 +-0.50

support_tape_length.source: Raspberry Pi RP-008146-DS-1, standard-standard 200 mm camera cable: support length 6.300 +-0.50

mass_per_length.source: computed: 15 x 0.7 x 0.027 mm copper + 16 x 0.11 mm PET film

modulus.source: PLACEHOLDER: homogeneous laminate modulus; fit from cantilever tests

tail_link_length.source: modelling choice: 12 x 6 mm of tail; the rest hangs free and is dropped

contact_pitch.source: Raspberry Pi documentation: standard camera interface, 15 positions at 1 mm

opening_width.source: TE customer drawing C-1734248 rev E1, 15 positions (likely Pi 4 CSI/DSI part 1-1734248-5): DIM C = 16.40 +-0.1 (read as the FPC opening)

seat_depth.source: TE customer drawing C-1734248 rev E1, 15 positions (likely Pi 4 CSI/DSI part 1-1734248-5): section X-X, 3.45 from the top face to the stop

slot_height.source: PLACEHOLDER: header 0.309 + 0.1 above and below; open-slot height is not on the drawing

top_leadin_half_length.source: PLACEHOLDER: funnel above and below the slot, 25 deg; typical ZIF housing

side_leadin_half_length.source: PLACEHOLDER: drawing shows corner chamfers at the pocket ends, undimensioned; 0 = straight walls

cable_thickness_spec.source: TE customer drawing C-1734248 rev E1, 15 positions (likely Pi 4 CSI/DSI part 1-1734248-5): applicable FPC thickness 0.3 +-0.05

housing_friction.source: PLACEHOLDER: housing-on-cable friction; the per-episode randomization overrides it

jaw_length.source: design choice: thin jaws so they fit on the 2.85 mm of tape outside the seated slot

free_film_length.source: design choice: 0 for the tape grip; 3e-3 for the film grip (fails: tip pitches)

clamp_force.source: I: derived requirement: >= force ceiling x 1.5 margin / (2 x mu); replaces Lakshya's 0.36 N simulation preload, which slips

pad_friction.source: PLACEHOLDER: pad-on-film friction until the pull test

tool.grasp_model: friction joint: the header may slide along the cable axis in the jaws once tangential load exceeds 2 x mu x clamp

position_kp.source: PLACEHOLDER: stand-in for a Cartesian impedance controller

physics.gravity_source: D: Pi 4 CSI socket is vertical (Lakshya's hardware review); for the Pi Zero side-entry case gravity is along -z

timestep.source: measured on this Mac: <= 1 ms keeps a 0.3 mm tip from penetrating a 0.5 mm slot

control_hz.source: design target from Lakshya's architecture guide

friction.source: PLACEHOLDER: randomize 0.2 to 0.6 until the pull test

corner_depth_tolerance.source: Lakshya seating.py: all four tip corners deeper than seat depth minus this

over_insertion_tolerance.source: M: Lakshya used 0.05 mm; the twin's soft backstop contact penetrates about 0.1 mm per newton, so 0.25 mm covers the 1.5 N ceiling. A hard stop cannot be over-inserted physically

peak_force_limit.source: PLACEHOLDER: until the insertion-force curves exist

start_gap.source: modelling choice: tip starts this far before the mouth
